document.title: Transcription of CIA 1996 biographic sketch, 'Usama Bin Laden: Islamic Extremist Financier'
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Osama Bin Laden File
document.note: Typed transcription of the CIA's 1996 bio sketch of bin Laden as a financier of Islamic extremist activities.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
aliases: Usama bin Muhammad bin Awad Bin Ladin
persons.role: Financier of Islamic extremist activities; organizer of al-Qaida (Islamic Salvation Foundation); businessman in Sudan
organizations: Al-Hijrah for Construction and Development, Ltd.
persons.status_detail: Alive at time of document (1996); relocated to Sudan in 1991; Saudi citizenship revoked in February 1994

mentions.quote: Usama bin Muhammad bin Awad Bin Ladin is one of the most significant financial sponsors of Islamic extremist activities in the world today.
Bin Ladin relocated to Sudan in 1991, where he was welcomed by National Islamic Front (NIF) leader Hassan al-Turabi.

persons.name: Muhammad Bin Ladin
persons.role: Wealthy Saudi construction magnate; founder of the Bin Ladin Group

mentions.quote: One of some 20 sons of wealthy Saudi construction magnate Muhammad Bin Ladin – founder of the Kingdom’s Bin Ladin Group business empire

persons.name: Hassan al-Turabi
persons.role: Leader of the National Islamic Front (NIF) in Sudan

mentions.quote: where he was welcomed by National Islamic Front (NIF) leader Hassan al-Turabi

persons.name: Ramzi Ahmed Yousef
persons.role: Alleged mastermind of the February 1993 World Trade Center bombing; resident of Bayt Ashuhada guesthouse in Peshawar

mentions.quote: Ramzi Ahmed Yousef, the alleged mastermind of the February 1993 World Trade Center bombing, resided at the Bin Ladin-funded Bayt Ashuhada (house of martyrs) guesthouse in Peshawar

persons.name: Bakr Bin Ladin
persons.role: Eldest brother of Usama; condemned his extremist activities in March 1994

mentions.quote: condemnation leveled against him in March 1994 by his eldest brother, Bakr Bin Ladin

organizations.name: al-Qaida
organizations.notes: Organized by 1985 by Bin Ladin as the Islamic Salvation Foundation to finance recruitment, transport and training of Arab volunteers; network of recruitment centers and guesthouses in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan; funded camps in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

organizations.name: Bin Ladin Group
organizations.notes: Jeddah-based family construction empire founded by Muhammad Bin Ladin.

organizations.name: al-Gama'at al-Islamiyyah
organizations.notes: Egyptian extremist group; worked with al-Qaida on camps; trained at 'Kunar' camp.

organizations.name: al-Jihad
organizations.notes: Egyptian extremist group allegedly funded by Bin Ladin; trained at 'Kunar' camp.

organizations.name: National Islamic Front
organizations.notes: Ruling Sudanese Islamist movement led by Hassan al-Turabi; business partners with Bin Ladin and co-operated on training camps.

organizations.name: Al-Hijrah for Construction and Development, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Built the tahaddi road and Port Sudan airport; works with Sudanese military to transport and provision terrorists training.

organizations.name: Wadi-al-Aqiq Company, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Import-export firm with near monopoly on Sudan's major agricultural exports.

organizations.name: Taba Investment Company, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Worked with Wadi-al-Aqiq on agricultural exports.

organizations.name: Al-Themar al-Mubarakah Agriculture Company, Ltd.
organizations.notes: Agricultural company with large tracts near Khartoum and eastern Sudan.

organizations.name: Al-Shamal Islamic Bank
organizations.notes: Khartoum bank capitalized by Bin Ladin ($50 million) and wealthy NIF members.

organizations.name: Advisory and Reformation Committee
organizations.notes: London-based organization formed after Saudi citizenship revocation; issued over 350 pamphlets critical of the Saudi Government by July 1995.

organizations.name: Bayt Ashuhada
organizations.notes: Bin Ladin-funded guesthouse in Peshawar where Ramzi Yousef reportedly resided.

organizations.name: Saudi Government
organizations.notes: Held Bin Ladin's passport 1989-1991; revoked his citizenship Feb 1994.

organizations.name: INTERPOL
organizations.notes: Yemen reportedly sought its help to apprehend Bin Ladin in 1994.

organizations.name: Afghan mujahedin
organizations.notes: Arab volunteers fought alongside them; Bin Ladin financed Arab recruits.

events.description: Soviet invasion of Afghanistan; Bin Ladin says he arrived within days.
By 1985 Bin Ladin organized the Islamic Salvation Foundation, or al-Qaida.
Soviets withdrew; Bin Ladin returned to Jeddah; Saudi officials held his passport 1989-1991.
Bin Ladin relocated to Sudan, welcomed by Hassan al-Turabi.
Attempted bombings against some 100 US servicemen in Aden; perpetrators claimed Bin Ladin financed them.
World Trade Center bombing; Ramzi Yousef alleged mastermind.
Bin Ladin financed travel of 300 to 480 Afghan war veterans to Sudan after Pakistani crackdown.
Joint Egyptian-Saudi investigation revealed Bin Ladin's business interests funneled money to Egyptian extremists.
By January 1994 Bin Ladin was financing at least three terrorist training camps in northern Sudan with the NIF.
Riyadh revoked Bin Ladin's Saudi citizenship.
Bakr Bin Ladin publicly condemned Usama's extremist activities on behalf of the family.
Ramzi Yousef apprehended.
Al-Jihad member interview claims Bin Ladin helped fund group; Advisory and Reformation Committee had issued 350+ pamphlets.
Bin Ladin organizes the Islamic Salvation Foundation (al-Qaida).
After Soviet withdrawal Bin Ladin returns to Jeddah.
Saudi officials hold Bin Ladin's passport.
Bin Ladin relocates to Sudan, welcomed by al-Turabi.
Attempted bombings against U.S. servicemen in Aden; perpetrators claimed Bin Ladin financing.
World Trade Center bombing, allegedly masterminded by Ramzi Yousef.
Bin Ladin finances travel of 300-480 Afghan veterans to Sudan after Pakistani crackdown.
Joint Egyptian-Saudi investigation reveals Bin Ladin's businesses funneled money to Egyptian extremists.
Bin Ladin has begun financing three terrorist training camps in northern Sudan.
Riyadh revokes Bin Ladin's Saudi citizenship.
Bakr Bin Ladin publicly condemns Usama through Saudi media.
Al-Jihad member says Bin Ladin helped fund the group; Advisory and Reformation Committee has issued 350+ pamphlets by this date.

sources_cited: July 1995 interview with a leading member of al-Jihad
key_claims: Bin Ladin was one of the most significant financial sponsors of Islamic extremism, financing recruitment, transport and training of Arab volunteers in the Afghan war.
By 1985 he organized al-Qaida (Islamic Salvation Foundation) with family wealth and Gulf merchant donations.
In Sudan, under Turabi's NIF, Bin Ladin built business ventures and financed at least three training camps.
Bin Ladin funded Egyptian groups al-Jihad and al-Gama'at al-Islamiyyah, including the Kunar camp in Afghanistan.
Bin Ladin-funded Bayt Ashuhada guesthouse in Peshawar sheltered Ramzi Yousef.
Saudi Arabia revoked his citizenship in 1994 and his family publicly condemned him.
